mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation for each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention source jurisdiction: notarize the certified copy locally, then obtain an Apostille from the designated Apostille competent authority of that jurisdiction. For a non-Hague source jurisdiction: notarize locally, then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate with competence over the source jurisdiction. The Apostille and consular routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Existence) for each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or tax authority in the UBO's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention source jurisdiction: extract from the official registry, notarize, and affix an Apostille issued by the source jurisdiction's competent authority. For a non-Hague source jurisdiction: notarize locally and legalize through the Korean Embassy/Consulate with territorial competence. Use one route only; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Korean formation agent and local registered representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed in a Hague Apostille Convention state: sign the resolution, notarize the signatures, and attach an Apostille from the competent state authority. If executed in a non-Hague state: notarize the signatures and complete consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document) of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate UBO and its authorized officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention source jurisdiction: certify the copy as true by a notary and obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority. For a non-Hague source jurisdiction: certify the copy by a notary and obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy/Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternate, exclusive routes; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each UBO's principal bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking bank maintaining the UBO's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention source jurisdiction: have the bank officer's signature notarized and then submit the notarized letter to the relevant Apostille competent authority. For a non-Hague source jurisdiction: have the bank officer's signature notarized and then submit the notarized letter for consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. Only one of the two routes applies; they are not sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, shareholders holding 25% or more, authorized signatories, and material counterparties must be screened before filing against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea designations administered by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Politically Exposed Persons, their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Any positive match or ambiguous discrepancy must be escalated to the Korea FIU and the transaction paused until cleared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-registry) and the local district court registry office serving the intended registered address
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be in Korean Hangul; a Latin-script transliteration may be used as a supplemental trade name for cross-border contracts and bank account references. The name must follow the four-tier Korean naming convention: (i) a distinctive element, (ii) an industry or business-object descriptor, (iii) the legal form designator 'Chusik Hoesa', and (iv) a locality or administrative-district disambiguator where necessary. A foreign-language-only name is not registrable as the sole corporate name; the transliteration must be the phonetically direct equivalent of the Hangul name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or counsel should obtain the written refusal notice from the district court registry and file a written objection or application for re-examination with the registry judge within two weeks. The objection must attach the i-registry name search records, explain the distinctive elements, and argue that no identical or deceptively similar name exists in the same business category. If re-examination is denied, an immediate appeal may be filed with the relevant High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. There is no statutory extension of the 30-day reservation window; the applicant should parallel-file an alternative name reservation to avoid delay while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not accepted by the National Tax Service, the district municipal tax office, or commercial banks for a Chusik Hoesa operating a creator MCN agency. The Commercial Act requires a registered head office address in the articles of association, and the Corporate Tax Act and VAT Act require an actual place of business for tax-invoice documentation and accounting records. Banks require a physical office inspection and reject foreign-controlled entities that rely only on a virtual office. A licensed serviced office or business-incubator lease may be accepted if the lease is in the company's name, the office is staffed and equipped, and the company can demonstrate local management control.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection checklist: corporate signboard, notarized lease agreement in the company name, employees enrolled in the four major social insurance systems, domestic corporate bank account, tax invoice ledger and VAT records, creator management contracts, IT equipment, records of director and shareholder meetings, and evidence of actual managerial control. Quantified risk: for a foreign-owned newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa in the digital-content industry, there is a 30-40% probability of an on-site verification by the district tax office or municipal licensing authority within the first 12 months; the probability rises above 45% if the first advance VAT return reports zero revenue or no local employees.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as most recently amended, particularly Articles 288, 289, 292, 295, 296, 301, 317, 318, 362, 383, 389, 393 and 401-2; the Commercial Registration Act; and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident investors
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office, filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System (Interet Deunggi) or in-person at the competent court registry (Sangbeop Deunggiso)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) under Article 317(1) of the Commercial Act, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation and the bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the current Korean Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation must state the authorized shares and issued shares, and the full subscription price of all issued shares must be deposited in cash into a restricted escrow account at a licensed Korean bank in the name of the company being formed. The bank will block release of the funds until the incorporation registration is completed and a certificate of incorporation is issued. Non-resident investors may hold 100% of the shares after reporting the investment to KOTRA or a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY], LTD. RESOLVED at a duly convened meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company], Ltd. (the Company) held on [Date] at [Time] at the Company's registered office and by video conference, with all incumbent directors present, that the Chairman declared a quorum and that the meeting was validly constituted under Article 368 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Company's Articles of Incorporation. After deliberation, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONFIRMATION. The Board confirms that the Company has validly issued [Number] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [Amount] per share, for an aggregate paid-in capital of KRW [Amount]. The Board accepts the subscriptions of each incorporator and confirms that the full subscription price has been paid in cash into the restricted escrow account maintained at [Bank, Branch], account number [Account]. The Board directs the Representative Director to obtain release of the escrowed capital immediately upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation by the competent District Court Registry. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates [Bank, Branch] as the principal deposit-taking institution of the Company and authorizes the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or severally as required by the bank, to open, operate, and maintain corporate bank accounts; to apply for internet banking credentials; to enroll the Company in creator payout settlement programs, including TikTok Creator Payout and Wise B2B payment rails; and to execute bank mandates, anti-money-laundering declarations, know-your-customer certifications, and electronic settlement agreements in forms acceptable to the financial institution. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts the address [Full Address] as the registered office and principal place of business of the Company for all statutory, tax, banking, and judicial purposes, and confirms that such address is within the registration jurisdiction of the [Name] District Court Registry. The Board directs the Corporate Secretary to file the registered office in all public registers and to maintain the corporate seal and minute books at that location. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints the following statutory officers with immediate effect: [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] as Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer; [Name] as Compliance and Anti-Money-Laundering Responsible Officer; and [Name] as Corporate Secretary. The Representative Director shall have general signatory authority, and bank account instructions, material contracts, and incorporation completion documents shall require the joint signature of the Representative Director and Chief Financial Officer where required by law or banking policy. 5. DELEGATION AND IMPLEMENTATION. The Board authorizes and directs the officers, legal counsel, and licensed filing agents to execute, notarize, apostille, file, and deliver all applications, declarations, appointments, and instruments needed to implement these resolutions, and any single officer may delegate administrative filing tasks to professional counsel or government filing representatives.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea Internet Registration System for name search; local licensed Notary Public in the intended district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name and trade-name availability search on the Supreme Court Internet Registration System to ensure that the proposed Korean and English names are not identical or confusingly similar to an already registered company. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, covering all mandatory particulars under Article 289 of the Commercial Act: corporate purpose, corporate name, total authorized shares, par value, registered office address, number of issued shares, method of public notice, and number of directors. The incorporators must sign and seal the Articles. Submit the signed Articles to a notary public for certification; the Articles become effective only upon notarization. If a foreign incorporator is represented by an agent, attach a notarized and apostilled power of attorney and certified passport copies of each foreign director and shareholder.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Corporate name availability search result or audit trail from the Supreme Court registry system
Valid passport or national ID of each incorporator
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if a formation agent is used
Proposed registered office lease agreement or owner's written consent to use the address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry name search identifies a conflict, amend the Articles or select a secondary corporate name and re-notarize. If the notary queries a missing mandatory provision, correct and re-paginate the Articles, and obtain a revised notarial certificate before proceeding to capital deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report and Blocked Paid-In Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea and licensed Korean foreign-exchange banks under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before inward remittance, file a foreign investment report with Invest Korea or a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank if any incorporator is a non-resident. The report must state the investor identity, capital amount, shareholding ratio, corporate purpose, and registered office. After the report is accepted, remit the full paid-in capital from the overseas shareholder into a restricted incorporation escrow account or temporary account opened in the name of the company being formed at a licensed Korean bank. The bank will mark the account as blocked and will not permit withdrawal before incorporation registration. Obtain the bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit certifying the company name, capital amount, number of shares, and payment date; this certificate is an indispensable annexure to the incorporation registration application. Complete all anti-money-laundering and source-of-funds declarations.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report Form and certificate of acceptance from KOTRA or the foreign-exchange bank
Overseas remittance instruction and bank payment confirmation
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued by the Korean bank
Share subscription declaration of each promoter
Beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds statement
AML/KYC forms for all shareholders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or KOTRA queries the foreign investment report, correct the shareholder organizational chart and source-of-funds documentation and resubmit within the statutory period. If the remittance is rejected for AML reasons, provide a bank-to-bank letter of origin and resubmit through the same licensed foreign-exchange bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Commercial Registration Division having jurisdiction over the registered office, including online submission through the Supreme Court Internet Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the capital deposit certificate, prepare the incorporation registration application on the prescribed judicial form. Pay the registration license tax, calculated at approximately 0.4% of paid-in capital, plus the local education surcharge, through the court payment system or tax office. Submit the application and all annexures to the competent District Court Registry in person or online. The registrar will examine the compliance of the Articles, the validity of share subscription, the sufficiency of the paid-in capital deposit certificate, the acceptance of office by each director and auditor, and the registered office proof. Upon approval, the Company is registered in the commercial register and comes into existence as a juridical person under Articles 317 and 318 of the Commercial Act. Request the certificate of corporate registration and a certified copy of the commercial register for subsequent banking and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation on the prescribed court form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit
Written acceptance of office by each director and statutory auditor if appointed
Share subscription statements or promoters' subscription records
Registered office proof, lease copy, or owner consent
Personal seal and identification of each officer
Receipt of payment of registration license tax and education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure the stated defect within the allowed grace period, usually two weeks, by uploading the requested document or explanatory memorandum. If the defect is substantive, withdraw the pending application, prepare corrected annexures, and refile with a new registration application and any additional fee required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Enrollment with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered head office, using the HomeTax online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File business registration with the National Tax Service within twenty days after incorporation registration. Complete the prescribed business registration application stating the corporate name, representative director, registered address, principal business purpose classified as ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810, advertising and creator agency activities, expected taxable period, and bank account details. Attach the certificate of corporate registration, corporate seal certificate, and lease agreement. The tax office will issue the business registration certificate and corporate tax identification number, which are required for value-added tax invoicing and corporate income tax filing. Also register for the electronic tax invoice system and, if required, appoint a domestic tax representative.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration from the court registry
Completed business registration application under the Value-Added Tax Act
Representative director's identification
Corporate seal certificate or seal impression certificate
Copy of the registered office lease agreement
Foreign investment report certificate if non-resident shareholders exist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects the business registration due to a mismatch in registered office or corporate purpose, correct the court registry record first or amend the business registration form and refile. Most corrections are resolved the same day through the HomeTax portal or the assigned tax officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Corporate Bank Accounts and Creator Payout Payment Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank compliance department, acting under the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit anti-money-laundering regime and the Financial Services Commission regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of corporate registration and the business registration certificate, attend the designated bank in person with the company dossier to convert the escrow account into the operating account and activate corporate internet banking. The bank will conduct a comprehensive know-your-customer and beneficial ownership review, screen directors and shareholders against sanction lists, and require specimen signature cards. The Representative Director and Chief Financial Officer must execute dual-approval mandates and set withdrawal limits. After account activation, enroll the Company with TikTok Creator Payout and Wise B2B by completing know-your-business verification, providing the corporate bank details, tax identification number, business registration certificate, and director identification, and passing the platform beneficiary verification. Maintain a compliance file containing all onboarding records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Business registration certificate
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Director and officer passport or national ID copies
Beneficial ownership register and source-of-funds statement
Registered office lease agreement
Bank mandate and anti-money-laundering compliance forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank holds approval due to beneficial ownership discrepancies or sanctions screening false positives, submit a corrected beneficial ownership declaration and a corporate organizational chart, and obtain a clearing letter from the relevant compliance officer. If TikTok or Wise rejects the onboarding application, provide the additional KYC/KYB documentation requested or use Wise B2B as a bridge payment route while reapplying.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 7310 Advertising and Creator MCN Agency is a digital services, creator representation, and consulting activity; no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are conducted, and no Environmental Impact Assessment, environmental registration, or pollution discharge permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there is no covered wastewater discharge point, VOC emission source, or hazardous waste generation in a pure digital creator agency operation. General commercial office waste and sanitary wastewater are managed through municipal collection, the local office building management, and the Sewerage Act through the municipal sewer system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit or industrial process safety license is required for a digital MCN agency. The leased commercial office must, however, be covered by the building owner's certificate of completion and basic fire and evacuation compliance under the Building Act and the Fire-Fighting System Installation and Maintenance Act, and the Company must enroll employees in the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance scheme at the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service when hiring staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with the online electronic portal HomeTax at hometax.go.kr; export customs clearance is administered by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa, the foreign or domestic promoter must register the corporation for business tax purposes with the competent NTS district tax office through HomeTax or in person immediately upon incorporation, using the corporate registration record, articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, lease or title proof for the registered place of business, director identification documents, and shareholder details. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the unified taxpayer identification number for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and national tax filings. For a non-resident foreign entity, the foreign company must register as a foreign corporation with a Korean domestic place of business within two months of establishing the place of business, appoint a Korean tax representative if required, and file the business registration application with HomeTax or the district tax office, attaching the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, constituent documents, apostilled or consular-legalised proof of existence from the home jurisdiction, evidence of the Korean place of business, board resolutions relevant to the establishment, and written authorisation for the tax representative. The NTS then issues the same 10-digit Business Registration Number for all Korean tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. The only relevant statutory election for a Chusik Hoesa is the consolidated corporate taxation system, under which a qualifying resident parent corporation and its wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries may make a group election to file a consolidated corporate income tax return under the Corporation Tax Act. Separate prescriptive elections for special tax deductions and credits are made directly on the corporate tax return; no entity classification election is available for indirect VAT purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary turnover registration threshold under Korean VAT law: every entrepreneur, including a Chusik Hoesa or its domestic taxable place of business, supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register for VAT regardless of annual revenue. A simplified taxable person regime exists for small businesses with annual taxable supplies not exceeding KRW 80 million, but this affects the filing form and input VAT credit method and does not exempt registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses must issue all tax invoices electronically through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice module or through NTS-approved ASP electronic invoicing providers; enterprise resource planning systems may connect via secure official APIs / machine-to-machine interfaces to transmit invoice data to the NTS in near-real-time. Each electronic tax invoice is assigned an NTS approval number upon transmission, and the system supports anti-fraud controls such as cross-matching between purchasers' and suppliers' e-invoices, HomeTax reconciliation, and real-time monitoring of suspicious zero-rated issuance. There is no physical fiscal stamping device in Korea; the mandatory e-invoicing obligation operates as the fiscal clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: zero-rating applies to exports of goods when the goods are physically removed from Korea and the export is evidenced by an export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service. For services: qualifying services supplied to foreign residents or overseas entities, including creator management and MCN agency services supplied to TikTok platforms or non-resident creators, are zero-rated when the service is contractually performed for a non-resident, the actual benefit and economic use occur in a foreign country, and the consideration is received in foreign currency or from foreign funds. The supply must be disclosed as a zero-rated supply with a zero-rated tax invoice issued in HomeTax, and the corresponding refund is obtained by deducting input VAT on related costs in the semi-annual VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korean Customs Service Export Declaration and export clearance certificate, available electronically in UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Korea to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice, export contract, or written service agreement signed with the overseas TikTok platform or foreign creator entity
Zero-rated VAT tax invoice issued through NTS HomeTax, clearly marked as zero-rated foreign earning service
Foreign exchange purchase certificate, inward remittance certificate, or bank receipt evidencing actual receipt of foreign-currency consideration

Foreign currency remittance record and TikTok creator payout / platform monetisation reports substantiating that the economic benefit arose outside Korea and that the performance and beneficial use occurred abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS together with Korea Customs Service will reconstruct export flows, verify customs export declarations, transport documents, foreign currency receipt records, and service performance evidence for every zero-rated export claim. If the required documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or if the foreign-currency proceeds are not repatriated within the prescribed period, the zero-rating is reversed, the supply is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply, VAT at 10% is assessed, and statutory additional taxes for non-declaration, under-declaration, or unfaithful tax invoices are imposed, typically up to 40% of the tax amount, with further interest and penalties for late payment. Fraudulent export refund claims or deliberate false documentation can trigger criminal tax-evasion penalties, including imprisonment up to three years or fines up to KRW 30 million, as well as joint collection liability against officers and controlling shareholders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) is the central bank; exchange control powers are administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) with BOK acting as the operational agent under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-floating foreign exchange regime with full current-account convertibility and a managed capital-account liberalisation. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, cross-border settlements for business operations (royalties, platform service fees, profit repatriation) are generally unrestricted but require timely reporting to a designated Korean Foreign Exchange Bank. Capital transactions, including foreign direct investment equity injections and capital reductions, are subject to a declaration regime; prior approval from the MOEF is still required for certain sensitive flows (e.g., strategic industries). There is no mandatory surrender requirement on export proceeds; exporters may keep foreign currency balances in domestic deposit accounts, although the proceeds must be repatriated within statutory timelines to support settlement accounting. Profit remittance for a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa is allowed through the Korea Investment and Financing Window, provided the original FDI report, audited financial statements, and withholding tax clearance are presented. In practice, individual wire transfers above USD 50,000 trigger additional AML review and documentary verification; higher-value remittances require bank compliance committee sign-off, but no material delays occur for properly documented treasury operations. The KRW is a freely convertible currency in the global market, though offshore non-resident speculative positioning in the onshore FX market is tightly supervised. Overall, the system is operationally open, with the main friction arising from rigorous document authenticity checks rather than convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to Korea within six months from the date of customs clearance (or service completion, as applicable) and must be credited to a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank account. The exporter must submit a settlement declaration to the receiving Foreign Exchange Bank within thirty days of receipt. There is no mandatory conversion into KRW; the foreign currency proceeds may be held in an eligible foreign currency deposit account. If the exporter has obtained local currency trade finance, repatriated proceeds must be converted to KRW to repay the trade loan. The Bank of Korea may grant extension for delayed repatriation upon written application with substantive justification (e.g., trade dispute, litigation).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Direct Investment Capital Escrow Account
Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise B2B, Airwallex) are not licensed under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act as settlement institutions able to hold Korean Won balances or connect directly to Korea's interbank clearing system. Consequently, the Chusik Hoesa cannot rely on an EMI for its primary treasury operations, including KRW payroll, VAT settlement, and corporate tax payments. EMIs can serve only as supplementary inbound/outbound facilitation through hosted partner-bank rails, with the usual three-to-five-day correspondent delay. The viability for primary banking is Low, and for cross-border payout backup it is Medium, subject to a full KYC being performed on the Korean entity and authorised signatories.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean anti-money laundering and real-name financial transaction regulations strictly require identity verification of the beneficiary beneficial owners and statutory directors. While a fully remote online opening is not acceptable, most top-tier Korean commercial banks accept a hybrid path: the statutory director or a duly authorised attorney-in-fact must present in person at the bank branch for one initial verification step, or, if residency abroad, complete a consular notarised power of attorney and a video interview with the compliance officer. The capital escrow account for foreign investment, however, generally requires the physical presence of one of the founders or an authorised officer during the investment certification procedure at a domestic branch of the Foreign Exchange Bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain lacks transparency with shareholding routed through a low-disclosure offshore jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete ownership structure chart down to each natural person, an up-to-date corporate registry extract (with apostille or consular legalisation), valid passports of all beneficial owners, the Investment Report already filed with the MOEF, and an independent professional legal opinion confirming no PEP status within the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: TikTok MCN revenue streams show a high volume of small-value credits from Singapore, triggering pattern-recognition red flags for potential funds layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish the fully executed TikTok Creator Agency Agreement, platform credential verification documents, 12 months TikTok earnings reconciliation statements, breakdown of creator pool payment calculations, and a signed auditor affidavit on revenue integrity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection to be made by a US company that has been in existence for less than 12 months or is domiciled in a high-risk state.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit source-of-funds affidavit from the investing company, three-month corporate bank statements, certified copy of the IRS Form including company formation certificate, board resolution authorising the investment, and a notarised deed of personal guarantee from the ultimate beneficial owner if requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The intended statutory director has a previous residency history in a jurisdiction associated with foreign exchange control penalties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply an official tax/residency clearance certificate from that jurisdiction, a written self-declaration on prior compliance record, evidence of residence termination, and a quarantine-stage enhanced due diligence package compiled by a licensed financial crime lawyer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial equity injection, the remitter must send an SWIFT MT103 using overseas direct investment purpose code (FDI) and must include the name of the Korean receiving bank, the Chusik Hoesa's investment account, and an explicit narrative referencing the MOEF FDI acknowledgement number. The Korean bank will verify the incoming credit, capture Foreign Exchange Transaction data, and issue a capital verification certificate (Customary Capital Verification) to the company within one business day. If the source country has a capital control regime, the remitter must provide local central bank clearance proof. All inbound settlements must pass through an authorised Korean Foreign Exchange Bank; receiving into a fintech EMI is not permissible.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recurring creator royalties and service fees to overseas entities are payable via SWIFT MT103 with the correct international service code (e.g., 3210 for creative content licensor fees). For larger procurement or service performance guarantees, a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by the Korean bank provides contractual settlement assurance. Documentary collections (DP/DA) are acceptable for low-value, longstanding vendors. Every outbound payment must be matched against the Korean withholding tax deposit certificate submitted to the National Tax Service; for royalties, the standard 20% withholding is applied and the remittee shall provide a tax exemption certificate from the relevant DTA if applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward foreign exchange contracts with mandatory real exposure documentation and a 10% margin on notional amount for Chusik Hoesa

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in KRW are permitted at authorised banks only when the counterparty evidences an underlying trade or FDI transaction; speculative NDF transactions are prohibited by the Financial Services Commission
Currency swap agreements (CNY/KRW and USD/KRW) are admissible for hedging balance-sheet foreign exchange risk subject to a statement of hedge accounting under K-IFRS 1022
Exchange-traded currency options on the Korea Exchange (KRX) limited to hedging operational cash flows, not available for market-making purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of audited financial statements, statutory auditor's report, and annual accounts under Articles 365-368 of the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART for audit-subject companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened by March 31 immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be disclosed on DART within 15 days after the AGM, and no later than April 15 in practice for standard year-end companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene AGM or file audited statements triggers fines up to KRW 5 million under Article 635 of the Commercial Act, FSS corrective orders under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, public disclosure of non-compliance, and in persistent cases referral to the court for compulsory dissolution or administrative strike-off of the corporate registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year end, being within 3 months of fiscal close; a 30-day ex officio extension is available for companies undergoing statutory external audit, with further special extensions for international tax or transfer-pricing filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or understatement triggers an additional tax of 20% of the understated corporate tax, plus daily delinquency interest of 0.03% (0.025%/0.022% tiered) on unpaid principal; persistent non-filing leads to NTS seizure of bank accounts, business assets, or tax receivables, and criminal referral for tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Declaration on Corporate Settlement (Jibang Sodeukse)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government authority (Si/Gun/Gu) where the head office is registered, processed through the local tax collection system linked to NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 following the corporate income tax return deadline for a December 31 fiscal year end; if corporate tax return is extended, the local return deadline shifts to the end of the following month of the extended corporate due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underdeclared local income tax attracts a 20% additional tax, a standard 5% late filing negligence surtax, daily delinquency interest of 0.03% on unpaid local tax, and administrative collection including garnishment of wages, deposits, and receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report Submission to Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART electronic disclosure system; report copy also delivered to the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must sign and deliver the audit report to the company so that it can be presented at the AGM; the auditor must then file the audit report with FSS/KICPA within 2 weeks of acceptance, which in standard December year-end calendar typically requires DART filing by April 14-15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure by the auditor to file, or company obstruction, results in administrative fines up to KRW 20 million, suspension or revocation of the CPA's audit registration, publication of the auditor's default in the official FSS bulletin, and referral of the company's directors to the court for administrative strike-off of the entity register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Status Report (when the Chusik Hoesa is FDI-qualified, e.g., foreign shareholder holds at least 10% or KRW 100 million investment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or through designated foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 of the calendar year following the fiscal year end for a December 31 year-end company; for off-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is June 30 of the year immediately following the close of that fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual FDI status report incurs an administrative fine up to KRW 1 million, and more importantly the entity can lose its 'foreign-invested company' status, thereby forfeiting tax incentives, customs exemptions, and legal protections under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory for a Chusik Hoesa when (a) total assets at fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); or (b) the company qualifies as a public-interest entity, a listed issuer, or a company designated by the Financial Services Commission due to business scope, industry significance, or cross-border investor protection; or (c) the company meets any two of the following three criteria: total assets at or above KRW 7 billion, annual revenue at or above KRW 10 billion, and 100 or more employees on average. A global TikTok MCN or creator incubation agency must also be audited if the economic owner or overseas head office requests an audited consolidation under its home-country accounting group rules, regardless of Korea's minimum size thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed entities and public-interest companies; private Chusik Hoesa entities may apply K-GAAP (Korean General Accepted Accounting Principles) as set out in the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the FSS accounting procedures, but may voluntarily adopt K-IFRS if parent guarantees control. Financial statements must provide a true and fair view and be prepared using the historical cost or fair value bases prescribed by the FSC regulation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea has no public beneficial-ownership register for private stock companies, but the Chusik Hoesa is required by the Commercial Act to maintain a continuous shareholder register and to amend it promptly when shares are transferred, pledged, or redeemed. For non-resident shareholders, any acquisition, disposal, transfer, or pledge of shares is reportable to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or a designated foreign-exchange bank within 30 days of the event. On an annual cycle, the board must present an updated shareholder list at the AGM, and the statutory auditor or external CPA must test the share transfer register and minutes as part of the audit; if the company is engaged in creator payments exceeding KRW 10 million per transaction, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) reporting rules require verification of beneficial identity and the annual confirmation of AML-risk profile for the MCN agency's banked payment rails.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors and Audit Committee
Register of Charges, Mortgages, and Pledged Shares
Corporate Minute Book for General Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 - 38,000 for a statutory CPA audit; USD 5,000 - 12,000 for a voluntary agreed-upon procedure or reviewed financial package if the entity remains below mandatory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: South Korea national corporate income tax: 9% on tax base up to KRW 200 million; 19% over KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% over KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion. A local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of national CIT is added, making the aggregate top statutory rate 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include: foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones can obtain full exemption from national and local corporate income tax for 5 years and 50% exemption for the following 2 years under the Tax Incentive Control Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act; R&D expenditure credits of up to 50% of qualifying creative/technology R&D expenses; SME tax reduction and exemption schemes; and reduced rates for income from qualified Korean digital content / creator incubation industries. No classic patent box is available, but tax credits may push the effective rate into the mid-teens for qualifying MCN startups.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return filed under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr). The operative form is the corporate tax base and amount declaration (NTS Form 10).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final corporate income tax return; semi-annual preliminary corporate tax payments are required for corporations whose prior-year tax payable exceeded KRW 5 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the end of each fiscal year, e.g. by 31 March for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa; consolidated corporations have four months from fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer identification and foreign shareholder declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registration number, corporate name, head office address, business area code, and the proportion of shares held by each non-resident shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate foreign beneficial owner and direct shareholding percentage. Include entity-level declarations required for Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting. Failure to state foreign ownership may disable later DTA and foreign investor relief claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a - Tax base and world-wide income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less allowable deductions, yielding worldwide taxable income of the domestic corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean Chusik Hoesa is tax resident in Korea and must declare worldwide income. TikTok creator-management fees and commissions originating through foreign platforms and Wise B2B settlements must be aggregated here, with corresponding foreign tax credits reported in the foreign tax credit section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reveals intercompany management fees, advertisement services, royalties, loans, and transfers with non-resident related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the transfer pricing method applied, comparable data, and arm's length price. Attach Local File and Master File if aggregate cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 10 billion. Non-resident branch or agency arrangements in foreign markets must be evaluated for permanent-establishment risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid or withheld in source jurisdictions on the same income included in the Korean tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign withholding tax certificates, TikTok or Wise payment records, and DTA-resident proof. Credit is limited to Korean tax attributable to the foreign-source portion; the unused portion is available as carryforward for five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - Audit adjustments and transfer pricing corrections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Voluntary adjustments increasing or decreasing taxable income to reflect arm's length results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report voluntary transfer pricing adjustments under Article 66 of the Corporate Tax Act. Any increase to taxable income will attract daily overdue interest unless settled promptly. Use an advance pricing agreement or MAP filing to prevent double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees paid by the Korean company to foreign investors or counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each payee, indicate the statutory 22% aggregate WHT rate or the applicable treaty-reduced rate. Attach the Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership statement before claiming the reduced rate. The payer is primarily liable if withholding is omitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a non-declaration penalty of 10% of the unpaid corporate income tax. Understatements incur 20% of the understated tax, while fraudulent understatements incur 40%, plus daily overdue interest (approximately 0.022% per day under the Basic Act on National Taxes). Failure to submit related-party disclosure documents attracts separate TP documentation penalties. Willful concealment of taxable income is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million, plus civil collection against directors in a piercing scenario.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national corporate income tax WHT plus 2% local income tax surcharge, totaling 22% aggregate withholding on gross dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders. Treaty rates may reduce this to 5% or 10% for beneficial owners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced WHT rate under a bilateral DTA, the non-resident payee must file an Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction under a Tax Treaty with the National Tax Service before or at the time of payment. A Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, proof of shareholding period for dividend rates, and evidence that the recipient is not a pass-through entity must be attached. The Korean payer may withhold at the treaty rate after NTS approval; the supporting documents must be retained for five years for future examination.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory outbound WHT for royalties and interest is 20% national plus 2% local surcharge, aggregate 22%. Under most Korean OECD-pattern DTAs, royalties are commonly restricted to 10%, interest to 10% to 15%, and dividends to 5% for shareholdings of 25% or more and 15% for portfolio holdings, subject to substantive beneficial ownership and PPT compliance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is triggered when aggregate cross-border transactions with foreign related parties equal or exceed KRW 10 billion in a fiscal year. Country-by-Country reporting is required for multinational groups whose consolidated revenue is at least KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies substance-over-form and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Although Korea has no separate jurisdictional ESR, the DTA relief and Foreign Investment Promotion Act incentives require the Chusik Hoesa to demonstrate real commercial substance: a physical office, employees, actual strategic decision-making, and core income-generating activities in Korea. A shell entity with only title to TikTok contracts and no local operational functions is disregarded, and its treaty benefits may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Concealment of Foreign-Source Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally underreporting TikTok creator management commissions and creator payout streams by diverting revenue into overseas bank accounts or Wise B2B settlement rails without remitting the accounts receivable into the Korean Chusik Hoesa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, willful evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to KRW 100 million. The tax authority also imposes a 40% dishonesty underreporting penalty under the Basic Act on National Taxes plus daily overdue interest on the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the court pierces the corporate veil, directors are jointly liable for the corporate tax deficiency and may face attachment of personal assets, civil restitution of diverted funds, a departure ban placed by the National Tax Service, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing management services through a foreign affiliate in a zero-tax or low-tax jurisdiction without employees or functions, charging non-arm's length royalties or commissioning fees for TikTok creator contracts, and failing to prepare Local File, Master File, or CbCR upon crossing the KRW 10 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 66 of the Corporate Tax Act, the National Tax Service may re-compute the taxable income using an arm's length method and impose a transfer pricing adjustment penalty up to 10% of the understated tax base, plus document-related penalties and daily interest. Willful false documentation may trigger criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fraudulent TP documentation can be held personally liable for the re-assessed tax when the entity is found to be a sham. The NTS may block personal bank accounts and register departure restrictions, and the directors face corporate-veil-pierced civil restitution and incarceration for repeat offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse, Shell Company, and Withholding Tax Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing outbound dividends or royalties through an intermediary company in a favorable DTA jurisdiction without obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate, without proof of beneficial ownership, and without any real economic activity, in order to obtain a reduced WHT rate; or failing to withhold prescribed non-resident tax on distributed profits and IP-derived royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 and the Principal Purpose Test, treaty benefits are denied and the statutory 22% aggregate WHT will be applied retroactively. The Korean payer acting as withholding agent is liable for the unpaid tax, 10% additional WHT negligence penalty, and daily interest; criminal evasion may be charged if the scheme is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structured the shell entity or authorised non-withholding are regarded as withholding agents and can be personally sued for collection. The NTS may freeze, blacklist, and impose travel bans; personal criminal liability includes imprisonment for aiding tax evasion, and civil asset restitution will be ordered against directors who moved the funds abroad.
